rationale: PINS THE TYPE THE SOURCE WRITES on the two declaration forms the receiver-cut pricing found untyped, both measured through the production path before the fix (.tmp-probe/dartgate/typed-head-probe.mts): an ANONYMOUS CLOSURE's own parameter list and a TYPED for-in variable. Why the closure list was missed is a grammar fact, not a heuristic gap: tree-sitter-dart writes a closure as `function_expression parameters: (formal_parameter_list …) body: (function_expression_body …)`, so the body's PREVIOUS NAMED SIBLING IS the parameter list — the traversal was handing it over all along — and `extractParameters` then searched for a `formal_parameter_list` CHILD inside the node it was given, found none, and returned no parameters. The identical method parameter published `Element.poke` while the closure parameter published a bare `poke` carrying `receiverCause: receiverTypeUnknown`. `collectDartLocalTypes` had no `for_loop_parts` branch at all, so `for (Element e in xs)` bound the name and never read the type next to it. Both reads are now of a type the SOURCE writes: nothing here infers one, and the shapes that name no type are pinned as DECLINES (an untyped closure parameter, an untyped `var` for-in, and a Dart 3 pattern binding — the last is DARTGAP1's bucket and the type written INSIDE the record pattern must not start typing the pattern's names). The C-style `for` is guarded off by construction: its `for_loop_parts` has init/condition/update fields and no name/value pair, which is what the rule requires before it reads anything.

expectRelationships.note: case A, CONTROL — a METHOD parameter was already typed before this change (the signature sibling carries the list, and `extractParameters` was handed a signature). It is pinned so a fix that started reading closure lists cannot be confused with a fix that changed method parameters.

case B, THE FIX (block body). Before: `calls -> poke` with `receiverCause: receiverTypeUnknown`. The row's SOURCE is the enclosing named function: a closure is not a call context (the family contract publishes no locals as sources), which is why the pin is `from: closures` and not the closure itself.

case B, second half — a member READ through the closure parameter. Before, this was a bare `id` with `receiverCause: receiverTypeUnknown`; the `knownQualifier: head` marker is the same one a local var's typed read carries.

the closure parameter's declared TYPE is a type MENTION and was already published before this change — the fix moved the BINDING's type, and this row states that the reference pass was not the thing that was missing.

case D, THE SECOND FIX — a TYPED for-in variable. Before: bare `poke` + `receiverTypeUnknown`. The fixture writes all three spellings the grammar gives it (`Element e`, `final Element e`, `await for (final Element e …)`) and the count below pins that they emit ONE row, because that is what a rule that reads the source should do at three sites.

case B, the binding itself: a closure parameter is still published as a BINDING (`BINDING_SEP`, U+0000) and never as a declaration target. The fix gave the binding a TYPE; it did not give the family a new local symbol.

case F, CONTROL — an UNTYPED closure parameter `(element) => element.id`. Nothing in the source names its type, so the read STAYS bare with the typing-gap cause. This is the pin that stops the fix from turning 'a closure parameter exists' into 'a closure parameter has a type'.

cases G and H, CONTROL — an untyped `var` for-in and a Dart 3 pattern binding, both of which must stay bare. The pattern case is the sharper one: a type IS written inside `(int n, Element element)`, and reading it would type a binding DARTGAP1 re-scoped by measurement rather than by this rule.
